Only methods declared in sugar-flexbox/src, or inherited from a parent declared there, are listed. A type that extends a class outside that tree, such as \RuntimeException, does not show the methods of that class.

Viewport final readonly class

Immutable viewport wrapper over the canonical FormsViewport.

MethodSummary
static new(int $width = 80, int $height = 24): selfConstruct with default dimensions (80×24).
static fromContent(string $content, int $width = 80, int $height = 24): selfConstruct a content-carrying viewport. The factory verb is fromContent() (FBX-22): the old name read as the fluent with*Content setter and PHP happily resolved \$vp->withContent() to the static — silently rebuilding an 80×24 box and discarding the receiver's geometry. Instance content changes are self::withContent() (the instance setter, FBX-06 — the retired static BC seat of that name is gone, so a static call now fails with the engine's own "non-static method" Error).
withStickyHeader(int $rows): selfPin the FIRST $rows lines as a sticky header region. The count is an ARGUMENT POLICY door (FBX-30): negative refuses loudly naming the value — a silent clamp-to-0 here while Viewport::new() refuses a negative dimension was three-way inconsistency in one class. 0 is legal and means 'no sticky region'; the render-time cap to what the height can show stays a GEOMETRY clamp (lines 240/252 era pins), not an argument judgement.
withStickyFooter(int $rows): selfPin the LAST $rows lines as a sticky footer region. The count is an ARGUMENT POLICY door (FBX-30): negative refuses loudly naming the value — a silent clamp-to-0 here while Viewport::new() refuses a negative dimension was three-way inconsistency in one class. 0 is legal and means 'no sticky region'; the render-time cap to what the height can show stays a GEOMETRY clamp (lines 240/252 era pins), not an argument judgement.

CSS flexbox-like layout for terminal UIs.

MethodSummary

withJustify(Justify $justify): selfDistribute leftover main-axis cells (see Justify). Leftover exists only where no ratio item absorbs it, as in CSS.

FlexItem final class

A single item inside a FlexBox.

MethodSummary

Main-axis distribution of leftover cells in a FlexBox.

CellPad final class

Combined fit-then-pad for the render loops (finding-040).

MethodSummary

static pad(string $line, int $knownWidth, int $cells, string $side): stringPad a line of KNOWN width to exactly $cells on $side without re-measuring. Distribution matches core's padCenter to the space: an odd gap sends the surplus to the right.

SugarCraft\Flexbox\Table

Column final class

Column definition for a Table.

MethodSummary
static new(string $title, int $width): self
static make(string $title, int $width): self
withAlign(Align|string $align): selfPlace cells of this column. The SHARED vocabulary is the Align enum (FBX-25) — the same cases FlexBox::withAlign() takes — and the legacy 'left'/'right'/'center' strings still ride through a coercion at the door; they retire with 2.0.0. Anything outside both spellings throws (they used to fall through to 'left' silently).
static alignOf(Align|string $align): stringResolve either alignment vocabulary to the renderer's padding string. Start/Center/End map onto left/center/right; Stretch is FlexBox sizing language with no cell meaning here and refuses.
withStyle(string $ansiStyle): selfSet the SGR style applied to every data cell of this column at render (the cursor style is painted OVER this one on a cursor row — see Table::buildLines() — so the selected row stays visually dominant).
withFormatter(callable $fn): selfAttach a cell formatter: fn(string $storedValue, int $rowIndex) answering string or null (null keeps the raw value). The answer is checked at format time and a non-string return refuses with this column's title (FBX-35): an array would have silently became 'Array' under the old cast and a plain object died a stack-trace away from the offending formatter.
sorted(int $direction = 1, int $priority = 0): selfAuthor this column as a sort key. The direction is NORMALIZED to the header-arrow contract: > 0 renders as +1 (ascending), < 0 as -1 (descending), 0 clears the marker.
unsorted(): self
format(string $value, int $rowIndex): string
padded(string $value, int $rowIndex): string
sortDir(): int
sortPriority(): int

Table final class

Sortable, filterable data table renderer.

MethodSummary
static new(): self
withColumn(Column $col): selfReturns a new Table with $col appended; receiver unchanged.
addColumn(Column $col): self
withRow(array $values): selfReturns a new Table with one more row (values are matched to columns by index).
addRow(array $values): self
withSort(int $colIndex, bool $ascending = true): selfSort rows by column index.
sortBy(int $colIndex, bool $ascending = true): self
sortByNext(int $colIndex): selfToggle sort direction on column, or start ascending if different column.
withFilter(string $text): selfFilter rows by text (Unicode case-folded substring match: 'ärger' finds 'Ärger' and 'strasse' finds 'Straße'; full accent folding too when ext-intl is loaded).
filter(string $text): self
clearFilter(): self
withCursor(int $rowIndex): selfMove the cursor to $rowIndex of the materialized view.
setCursor(int $rowIndex): self
withCursorStyle(string $ansiStyle): self
withCursorMarker(string $prefix): selfNon-colour focus marker prepended to the cursor row's first cell.
withHeaderStyle(string $ansiStyle): self
withSeparator(string $s): selfSet the cell separator. The string is rendered raw between every pair of cells, so it is sanitized at ingress exactly like data cells: control sequences cannot ride the separator into the terminal (ruler jointing then measures the sanitized display width).
withRulerChars(string $fill, string $joint): selfTheme the ruler's two runes: the horizontal fill and the column joint (default '─' / '┬', byte-identical to every frame ever rendered). ASCII-themed tables mixed unicode rulers under ASCII separators until the ruler characters rode the same ingress as the separator: sanitized, and STRICTLY one cell — a multi-cell or zero-cell rune would desync the ruler line from the header width arithmetic that FBX-16/FBX-34 welded together, so the door refuses anything but a single-cell grapheme, loudly and by name.
withEmptyText(?string $text): selfPaint a spanning row when a filter ate every row (FBX-41).
withVisibleRange(int $from, ?int $to = null): self
rowCount(): int
colCount(): int
totalRowCount(): intRows SUPPLIED, before any filter or window: totalRowCount() > 0 with rowCount() === 0 is the 'no match' state; totalRowCount() being 0 is plain 'no data'. The pair is what lets an app paint its own empty-state row with different copy (FBX-41).
filterText(): stringThe active filter text ('' when unfiltered).
columns(): arrayThe column roster, index-addressed exactly as the sort keys and header render see it.
cursor(): ?intThe cursor's index in the materialized view, settling any pending sort/filter first — the same law as rawCurrentRow(). Null means the index addresses no visible row: with FBX-26's refused out-of-range cursors and the follow-its-row re-sort, the only reachable case is an empty view holding the default index 0.
rawCurrentRow(): ?arrayThe cursor row of the MATERIALIZED view, RAW: a pending sort or filter is settled first, so this always answers about what render() would show, not about the stale last-settled frame. Null when the view has no rows at all — an out-of-range cursor cannot exist to fall off (withCursor() refuses it, and re-sorts carry the selection with its row), so the empty view is the one honest null source.
rawCurrentCell(int $colIndex): ?stringOne cell under the cursor, RAW like self::rawCurrentRow() — the stored string with no sweep applied — or null when the cursor is off the view or the column index is out of range.
currentRow(): ?array
currentCell(int $colIndex): ?string
render(): stringRender the table to a full string (always full frame, never delta).
buildLines(): arrayBuild all rendered lines (header, separator, data rows).
computeTotalWidth(): intTotal display width of a rendered line, in CELLS: column widths plus the separator's display width at every joint. Byte counting the separator (strlen) over-reported any non-ASCII joint — ' │ ' is 5 bytes but 3 cells — and zero columns used to yield a negative total from the (n - 1) joint term.

TableRenderer final class
